sentences.text: Revenue was zero in FY2019 and FY2020 [F1][F2] and $55.0 million in FY2021 [F3], so the FY2022 to FY2025 compound rate of 48.1% [D342] is the usable measure.
The shape is a launch step change, then compounding that is now slowing [D239].
FY2022 revenue rose 2914.5% to $1,658 million [D83][F4], which the filing ties to 19,412 more vehicle deliveries [P67].
FY2023 revenue rose 167.4% to $4,434 million [D135][F5], which the filing attributes to higher deliveries and selling prices [P56].
In FY2025, Software and Services added +21.6pp [D295] to the 8.4% revenue growth [D239], while Automotive subtracted 13.2pp [D316].
The filing attributes Software and Services growth mainly to vehicle electrical architecture and software development services [P18], largely provided through a Volkswagen Group joint venture [P27].
Volkswagen Group revenue added +15.4pp [D281] to FY2025 growth, rising from 1.5% of revenue in FY2024 [D278] to 15.5% [D279].
Operating costs rose 6.9% [D258] against revenue growth of 8.4% [D239], so the operating loss narrowed 23.5% [D240].
Per-share loss fell 34.5% [D242], more than the 23.2% net loss reduction [D241], because the diluted share count rose 17.1% [D260].
At -66.5% [F31], operating margin is the window high [D325], but still well below the autos peer median of -1.6% [D344].
The 27.8pp operating margin gain [D253] is mostly cost of revenue, +26.8pp [D267], with R&D adding +1.5pp [D268] and SG&A subtracting 0.5pp [D269].
Cost of revenue fell 15.0% [D255] on fewer vehicles produced and delivered and lower raw material and conversion costs [P21].
SG&A rose 9.9% [D257] on go-to-market expansion, higher payroll and stock compensation [P13].
Other expense moved from -$7.0 million in FY2024 [X83] to -$54.0 million [X84], which the filing links to a $186 million settlement charge [P10].
Operating cash flow was -$779 million in FY2025 [F64], a 54.6% shrink in the outflow [D244] from -$1,716 million a year earlier [F63].
The filing attributes the smaller operating outflow to a significant reduction in the net loss [P4].
Free cash flow was -$2,489 million [F78], a -46.2% margin [D226], against a window median of -132.9% [D335].
Capital expenditure rose 49.9% to $1,710 million [D246][F71], or 2.18x D&A [D228], for expansion at the Normal Factory [P3].
Net cash fell to $1,642 million [D231] from $3,259 million in FY2024 [D179] and $4,937 million in FY2023 [D127].
At 30.5% of revenue [D232], net cash ranks at the 75th percentile of the four-company autos group [D351], against a peer median of 17.8% [D352].
The filing ties FY2025 financing mainly to share issuance to Volkswagen Group [P2], as diluted shares rose 17.1% [D260].
Cash and investments cover 2.4 years of burn [D236], down from 2.7 years [D184], so reliance on outside funding continues.
Net losses have appeared in each of the last seven years, reaching $3,646 million in FY2025 [F38][R1].
Stock-based compensation was 13.8% of revenue in FY2025 [D223], at least 10% for five years [R2], which the filing ties to accrued bonus incentives [P13].
New electric vehicles fell 12.5% [D287] and Automotive fell 14.6% [D315] [R4][R5], with the filing citing fewer deliveries after 45W credits expired [P22].
Amazon and Volkswagen Group, both principal owners, account for 16.7% [D275] and 15.5% [D279] of FY2025 revenue.
Gross margin of 2.7% [F19] is the window high [D331]; a fall back below zero, from -24.1% in FY2024 [F18], would show the cost gains reversing in the FY2026 10-K.
Cash and investments of $6,082 million [D229] cover 2.4 years of burn [D236]; a shorter runway in the FY2026 10-K would confirm rising reliance on outside capital.
Automotive revenue turning positive from -14.6% [D315], as R2 deliveries begin in the second quarter of 2026 [P31], would confirm the vehicle base is recovering.
